items.t: Co-chaired a successful 2011 statewide ballot campaign to restore same-day voter registration (2011).
items.q: co-chaired a successful 2011 statewide ballot campaign to restore same-day voter registration.

items.t: Says states, not the federal government, are in charge of elections.
items.q: Today’s ruling affirms that the states, not the federal government, are in charge of our elections.

items.t: Said she will continue to defend Mainers' voting rights and privacy.
items.q: I will continue to defend every Mainer’s voting rights and their privacy

items.t: Argued that the Department of Justice did not explain how it planned to use the Maine voter data it requested.
items.q: Bellows argued that the DOJ did not provide an explanation for how it planned to use the data they requested, which included the names of everybody on Maine's voter rolls

items.t: Said Maine law required her to hold a hearing and issue a decision after five voters challenged the ballot qualification of Donald Trump.
items.q: Five voters did so, including two former Republican state senators. And then I was required under the statute, under the law, to hold a hearing and issue a decision, and do so within a very compressed timeline.

items.t: Served as Senate Chair of the Labor and Housing Committee in the Maine Senate.
items.q: Secretary Bellows previously served two terms in the Maine Senate from 2016-2020, during which she served as Senate Chair of the Labor and Housing Committee and on the Judiciary Committee.

items.t: Said elected officials must reduce bureaucracy, improve efficiency and modernize systems.
items.q: It is incumbent upon us as elected officials to make government work for the people of Maine. We must reduce bureaucracy, improve efficiency, modernize our systems

record.t: Declined the US Department of Justice's request for Maine voter data in August 2025, after which the DOJ filed suit against Maine in September 2025.
record.q: Secretary Bellows first declined the DOJ's request in August 2025. The DOJ filed suit against Maine in September 2025.

record.t: Was sworn into office for a third term as Secretary of State.
record.q: Secretary of State Shenna Bellows was sworn into office for her third term today, Wednesday, January 8, 2025.

record.t: Chaired the Executive Committee of the Election Infrastructure – Information and Analysis Center from 2024 to 2025.
record.q: She serves on the national Executive Committee of the Election Infrastructure – Information and Analysis Center, which she chaired from 2024-2025.

record.t: Served as Senate Chair of the Labor and Housing Committee during her two terms in the Maine Senate from 2016 to 2020.

record.t: Serves as Maine's 50th Secretary of State and its first female Secretary of State.
record.q: Secretary of State Shenna Bellows is Maine’s 50th Secretary of State and first female Secretary of State.

record.t: Said she helped lead a coalition of states in response to the Department of Justice lawsuit against Maine.
record.q: When they tried to bully me by suing Maine, I helped lead of coalition of states to fight back – and we’re winning.

record.t: Removed Donald Trump from Maine's 2024 presidential primary ballot, declaring him ineligible under Section 3 of the 14th Amendment.
record.q: Former President Donald Trump was removed from Maine’s 2024 presidential primary ballot by Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows on Thursday, declaring him ineligible under Section 3 of the 14th Amendment.
